A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from Omni-DPO to Uni-DPO. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices provide sufficient readable evidence for comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments on textual, mathematical and multimodal benchmarks, together with ablations and training analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds downstream evaluations, expert-model ablations, training diagnostics and further comparisons.

M1.justification: The quality and performance weights, length normalization, calibrated NLL loss and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure. Renaming the method and documenting score construction more fully do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: New Section D.4 evaluates MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, Winogrande and CommonsenseQA, substantially expanding downstream task coverage. The existing instruction-following, mathematical and multimodal datasets and benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table D.5 adds Eurus2-SFT, Eurus2-PRIME, OpenReasoner-Zero-7B, SimpleRL-Zero-7B, Dr. GRPO and PPO comparisons while retaining the earlier principal comparators. New Table F.1 compares published β-DPO and D2PO results, and Table 1 adds a Gemma SFT baseline.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce periodic mathematical benchmark evaluation across three training epochs, controlled expert-scorer substitutions and downstream evaluation using Language Model Evaluation Harness. Existing greedy decoding and zero-shot mathematical pass@1 protocols remain; newly disclosed precision and sampling parameters do not establish changes to earlier runs.

E4.justification: Table D.9 newly tests dependence on expert-model strength. Figures C.1 and D.1 add loss, gradient, response-probability and benchmark-performance trajectories, while C.4 examines computational overhead. These substantially extend the earlier component ablations, sensitivity studies and overfitting analysis.

E5.justification: Table D.8 fills previously missing Arena-Hard confidence intervals for Llama3-8B-Instruct SFT and DPO. Table C.3 newly specifies seed 42 for mathematical and multimodal training. Existing uncertainty-reporting practices and single-run mathematical evaluation remain; additional independent runs are not established.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added through expanded comparisons, downstream tests, scorer ablations and training trajectories. Existing mathematical averages of 49.54 and 56.80 remain unchanged. New Table D.5 reports PPO at 56.84 versus Uni-DPO at 56.80, and Table D.10 reports both gains and regressions. Some previously missing SFT scores are also supplied.

T1.justification: Equation (9) removes the redundant external β factor, bringing it into agreement with the retained Appendix B.2 derivation, where β already enters through the reward-margin gradient. Section C.4 also adds a simple computational-overhead relation. The remaining principal derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains joint quality/performance weighting with calibrated NLL, claimed to improve preference optimization and generalization. The abstract now explicitly includes multimodal effectiveness, but that contribution was already claimed in v2's introduction and supported in its appendix.

C2.justification: Sections E.2–E.4 add explanations of base-model sensitivity to length normalization, c-NLL versus generic SFT loss, and focal-weight relaxation. New discussions interpret scorer independence and downstream capability changes, and assert that c-NLL avoids overfitting. Some interpretations are overly broad: D.4 describes consistent improvements despite regressions in Table D.10.

D1.justification: Section C.2 now documents FastChat scoring prompts, ArmoRM z-score/CDF conversion to 0–10, and mathematical sampling temperature and top-p of 0.8. Training tables add bfloat16 and label-smoothing information; C.4 supplies FLOP/memory accounting. A reproducibility statement newly specifies release of data and training scripts. These substantially expand documentation without demonstrating changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section F.3 substantially expands positioning against adaptive weighting approaches, explicitly discussing β-DPO, D2PO, RDO, WPO, MWPO and RPO. Although β-DPO and RDO were already cited, their relationship to the proposed contribution is developed further. Additional RL-method and downstream-benchmark references accompany the expanded evaluations.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change to Uni-DPO, with edits to the abstract and introduction. Earlier E.1–E.3 material is consolidated into E.1, related work gains numbered subsections, and reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added. Most existing methodological prose, derivations and case studies remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the twelve-panel Figure C.1, performance-trajectory Figure D.1 and Tables D.9, D.10 and F.1. Table D.5 is expanded and reorganized by method category and result source. Figure 3 is revised, and conference formatting changes typography and placement throughout the document.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, clearer score-construction details, expert-dependence tests and training diagnostics improve reproducibility and empirical scrutiny. Broader comparisons are useful, but their reporting limits the gain: Table F.1 combines values from different Table 1 configurations, and summaries of Tables D.5 and D.10 overstate superiority. The retained main evidence and corrected gradient formula support a limited net improvement.
